message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
Because both regions observe daylight‑saving time, the gap can briefly shift:

| Period | LA offset | Berlin offset | Difference |
|--------|-----------|---------------|------------|
| Standard time (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 h** |
| After U.S. DST starts, before German DST starts | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **+8 h** |
| After both start DST | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **+9 h** |
| After Germany ends DST, before U.S. ends | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **+8 h** |
| After both end DST | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 h** |

So for most of the year Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles, but during the short windows when only one side has switched to daylight‑saving time the difference becomes 8 hours (or 10 hours if you’re looking at the reverse window in late summer/early fall).
